newsitem.title: USA: U.S. envoy to chair Kurdish talks next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy to chair Kurdish talks next week.

text.p: A senior U.S. envoy will chair direct talks in Turkey next week between rival Kurdish factions after helping arrange a ceasefire between them in Northern Iraq, the State Department said on Thursday.
Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said the ceasefire, agreed on Wednesday by the Kurdish Democratic Party (KDP) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), appeared generally to be holding.

"There were some reports of sporadic fighting but that may have been a case of some of the forces...not getting the word. It appears now the ceasefire is taking hold," Burns told a regular news briefing.

He said Robert Pelletreau, Assistant Secretary of State for Near Eastern Affairs, now visiting the Gulf, would return this weekend to Turkey, which borders Iraq, and initiate talks between the two Kurdish groups in the middle of the week.

"Both will be represented at the table with him and with representatives of the governments of Turkey and the United Kingdom," Burns said. Britain and Turkey have helped bring the two feuding factions together.

"We have hopes that these talks might lead the KDP and the PUK to maintain the ceasefire and to decide together on some form of political reconciliation so that the situation in Northern Iraq can be more stable and more peaceful," he said.
